report_text: The Guardian dashboard for 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-30 shows 482 articles across 10 countries. United Kingdom has the most raw coverage (118 articles), and Japan has the least (18). The raw gap is 6.6x, but the per-capita view shifts attention toward Australia (2.7 per 1M). Because this is only Guardian data, the result should be treated as an editorial attention measure, not a universal measure of country importance. A useful next step is to assign follow-up review to countries that are low in both raw and per-capita coverage. Researchers can use the dashboard to track whether these visibility gaps persist over time.

## Guardian Coverage Brief

From 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-30, the Guardian sample contains 482 articles across 10 countries, averaging 48 articles per country. The United Kingdom leads raw coverage with 118 articles, while Japan has 18, a 6.6x gap. Raw volume does not tell the whole story: Australia leads per capita at 2.7 articles per 1M people. Editors should review whether low-volume countries need additional context stories before concluding that Guardian attention reflects real-world importance.

Global attention is clearly biased and dramatic. Britain dominates because editors are obviously more interested in powerful countries, while Japan is almost ignored with only 8 articles. This proves a major media blind spot and shows that international reporting priorities are broken.
